key_insight: A spectrally regularized latent compression stage dramatically improves turbulence generation by preserving dissipation-range energy that standard MSE-trained latent models suppress.
engineering_relevance: This yields a better quality–cost tradeoff for CFD surrogate generation, enabling accurate synthetic turbulence at far fewer function evaluations.
method: Train a latent flow-matching generator with a zone-weighted log-spectral objective instead of plain MSE.
Use encoder-decoder swap experiments to isolate whether performance gains come from the latent representation or the decoder.
Evaluate spectral fidelity, deep-dissipation power retention, and structure functions for both reconstruction and unconditional sampling.
evidence_signal: On a 256^2 DNS dataset at Re_f ≈ 2250, deep-dissipation retained spectral power improved from 25% to 94% in reconstruction and from 20% to 79% in unconditional generation, with DD bias reaching -0.117 at 20 function evaluations.
watch_item: The models still show a residual gap in the magnitude of S_3, suggesting phase-coherent triadic structure is not yet fully captured.
paper_title: Spectrally Regularized Latent Flow Matching for Turbulence Generation
